defects.desc: The initial commit makes nodeview.InternalPointer refuse every '#name' fragment, so the pre-parse cycle scan drops $anchor edges the resolver does follow. A pure-$ref cycle through $anchor kills the process with an unrecoverable stack overflow. The #523 repro plus '$anchor: x-s' on A was refused as cyclic-ref at BASE and crashes at the initial commit. fafdb087 adds an over-approximating $anchor/$id/$defs reach check and refuses it again. Verified with built binaries: BASE exit 1 cyclic-ref, initial commit 'fatal error: stack overflow', fafdb087 exit 1 cyclic-ref. The plain anchor self-cycle crashed at BASE too and is also refused at fafdb087.
defects.review_quote: the cycle scan no longer sees `#name` edges, but the resolver follows some of them, so an anchor-based pure-$ref cycle kills the process with a fatal stack overflow. One shape the scan refused before this commit now crashes.

non_defects.reason: New scope and the PR's own titular change: it reads a $defs pointer from its own schema (#557). The $defs collapse existed before the initial commit, which did not introduce or touch it.
Merge of main into the branch, reacting to main moving (#541 and #563 squash-landed, plus #562, #564 and #565).

Fixes defects in code that 750d27db introduced: the cubic defs lookup, unreported dangling $defs refs, fragmentOf and MappingPointer, which do not exist at 3515599f. None of it was present in the initial commit.
Fixes memory growth in defs.Reader, which a later commit introduced.
Merge of main (#567) into the branch.
A refactor of the defs reader and its callers, introduced later, with no behaviour change.
Test coverage for the later $defs rule in operations and callbacks; continuation of the new scope.
Fixes quadratic per-reference GetJSONPointer searches in the defs rule, which a later commit introduced.
Pins $defs behaviour in aliased and merged schemas, with a positions.go tweak. Both belong to the later defs rule.

extras.finding: nit: the TestDetectCycles_AnchorFragmentIsNotWalked doc comment gives each case the other's job (the pointer twin is said to fail on a revert of the leading-'/' refusal)
extras.why: Confirmed by mutation at 3515599f: replacing the leading-'/' check with `if false` fails the anchor case and passes the pointer twin, the opposite of what the comment says. No truth commit in this PR touches it. #541's landed version (add31b04) rewrote the comment exactly as the review proposed.

extras.finding: nit: the commit message and test doc claim the two fragment readers agree on every same-document fragment and name one documented exception, but 'spec.yaml#/a' (self-named) disagrees: scan=("",false), lower=("/a",true)
extras.why: Reproduced with a probe test at 3515599f, which gave exactly that output. '##/a' is a second spelling of the bare-'#' exception. The divergence is harmless because the resolver rejects the self-named form, but the universal claim is inaccurate. Low severity, and the truth never fixed it.

extras.finding: suggestion: the 'load.go's resolveDiag, a separate issue' comment in TestCompile_NonUTF8FragmentReachesNoIdentifier cites no issue; file one and cite #N
extras.why: The site really was defective: it points to an issue that does not exist. The diagnosis was wrong, though. #541's landed version rewrote the comment to say diag.Newf scrubs the byte to U+FFFD by design, so the right fix was to correct the comment, not to file a defect. It counts as a real comment flaw, but following the review's advice would have filed a non-issue.

extras.finding: pre-existing: pure-$ref cycles through $anchor overflow the stack at BASE too (A: {$anchor: a, $ref: '#a'})
extras.why: Verified: the BASE binary also dies with 'fatal error: stack overflow' on this spec. It is the same mechanism as D1 and is fixed by fafdb087 (#526, #546).

extras.finding: pre-existing: a multipart body whose $ref does not resolve emits an encoding key that pass.Validate rejects (ir/encoding-key-unknown-property)
extras.why: Running the CLI with validation on a dangling multipart $ref at BASE gave only unresolved-ref errors and no encoding-key diagnostic, probably because validation does not run after error diagnostics. I did not run pass.Validate directly, so the claim is unconfirmed.

extras.finding: pre-existing: library resolver errors are located at the document root ('spec.yaml#') with no site
extras.why: Observed at BASE: 'mp.yaml#: not found -- key Missing not found in sequencedmap.Map'. The initial commit did not introduce it.

extras.finding: pre-existing: nodeview and resolve comments cite speakeasy v1.24.0 while go.mod pins v1.25.2
extras.why: Confirmed: go.mod pins v1.25.2 and the v1.24.0 citations are on lines the initial commit's diff does not change. The citation is stale but harmless, and the commit did not introduce it.

missed_patterns: The review caught the one defect the truth fixed in the initial commit, with a reproduced regression, so nothing was missed. One finding was weak: the review assumed an unexplained leftover in a test comment was a standing defect to file. Instead, the reviewer should check whether the behaviour is deliberate, for example a scrubbing helper like diag.Newf, before recommending an issue. Where it is deliberate, the fix is to correct the comment.
